item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Bina looks at the diagram of parallelogram $ABCD$. Angle $A$ is marked $65^{\circ}$.

Which claim correctly determines the adjacent and opposite angles?

options.A: Adjacent angle $B$ is $115^{\circ}$ (co-interior with $A$ on parallel sides), and opposite angle $C$ equals angle $A$, so $C=65^{\circ}$.
options.B: Call $ABCD$ a parallelogram even when the co-interior pair on parallel sides is not used to find angle $B$.
options.C: Equal adjacent angles produce parallelogram $ABCD$, so angle $B$ must also be $65^{\circ}$.
options.D: Apply equality of opposite angles also to a kite that is not a parallelogram, using only the printed $65^{\circ}$.
